result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly say that normal and out-of-range rooms get the same visual weight, tie this to the Room 5 incident, and put card-level alert treatment first. A does better on restraint: its first fix pairs a louder alert card with quieter healthy cards (no shadow, calmer numbers), while B only briefly mentions quieting healthy cards. B adds useful practical advice outside the design itself, such as checking the alert threshold and adding push alerts. Neither answer clearly says what to keep from the current page. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly find that alert and healthy rooms look almost the same, and both say the first fix is to change the whole card when a room is out of range. B goes further on quieting healthy cards: it removes the shadow, lowers the number weight and demotes 'days to harvest', so contrast comes from restraint as well as emphasis. B also gives a clearer, more specific fix order. A has useful extra points about checking the alert thresholds and adding push alerts, but it spends less effort on quieting the in-range state.
